title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-04-12
lineage: [SBD > Reel master > Sonic Solutions > DAT ] + [Aud > cassette master > PCM > DAT > Sonic Solutions] > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording of a high‑energy 1970 show, highlighted by a blistering Dancin' in the Streets and soaring Viola Lee Blues.
ai_review.review: The SBD capture is crystal‑clear with excellent presence and minimal tape noise, letting the band’s aggressive late‑summer 1970 vibe shine through.  The performance is driven by a monster Dancin', fat organ on Viola Lee, tight Deep Elem blues and a solid Black Peter, while the flow from Candyman into Viola Lee feels seamless.  Minor complaints focus on a few three‑second track gaps and a sloppy China→Rider transition, but overall the show is regarded as one of the standouts of the year.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly praise both musical performance and recording fidelity; weighted average (70 % show, 30 % recording) yields a rating in the high‑4‑range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with good instrument separation; occasional minor patch noise and three‑second gaps between tracks noted but not detrimental to listening.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Generally praised for smooth transitions (e.g., Candyman → Viola Lee) and a strong second‑half momentum; only the China→Rider segue is described as sloppy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for a snaky, blazing solo on Dancin' and a uniquely creative guitar voice throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for powerful bass work that drives the jams, especially during Dancin' and the deep organ moments; praised as “pounding out the jam”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ/keyboard presence is unusually forward – highlighted on Viola Lee, Deep Elem and Black Peter – though a few reviewers heard brief patch noise.
band_member_comments.Drums: Solid, steady foundation with occasional standout drum breaks noted in reviews.
